newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids mostly hold, USG low sulphur tanks.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids mostly hold, USG low sulphur tanks.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices, helped by firmer crude and gas markets, mostly held steady Tuesday in sluggish trade, but U.S. Gulf low sulphurs tanked amid aggressive selling interest and no demand.
"Some markets have stabilized, but there's still a lot of pressure on low sulphur, particularly in the Gulf," said one cash trader, adding USG high sulphur held steady today.
Traders said a large player aggressively offering one percent barrels in Houston helped tank USG low sulphur prices almost $1 a barrel to about $13.25.
USG three percent, helped by reports of a 60,000-barrel prompt sale at $12.05 (FOB Beaumont, Tx), held steady at $11.75-12.00, traders said.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $15.00-25, with March paper up more than 25 cents with crude to about $15. April paper saw similar gains and was quoted at about the same number.
High sulphurs in New York also were stable.
Traders said competitive city gate gas prices continued to drain utility demand from resid.

New York city gate swing gas prices eased slightly to $2.10/mmBtu, or about $13.23 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, gained more than five cents to about $1.85/mmBtu, or $11.66 a barrel equivalent.
